script.title: परशुराम ने सागर से धरती निकाली, फिर नागों को क्यों बुलाया 🤯
script.hook_text: परशुराम के फरसे से समुद्र हटा
sentences: मान्यता है, परशुराम के एक फरसे ने पूरा समुद्र पीछे धकेल दिया।
विष्णु के छठे अवतार ने महाराष्ट्र के साल्हेर किले से इसे अरब सागर में फेंका था।
केरल की कथा के अनुसार, गोकर्ण से कन्याकुमारी तक पानी घटा और नई धरती निकल आई।
मगर समुद्र से निकली उस ज़मीन में सिर्फ नमक ही नमक था।
तब इस ज़मीन को बचाने परशुराम ने नागराज वासुकी को बुलाया।
वासुकी के पवित्र विष ने बंजर धरती को उपजाऊ और हरा-भरा बना दिया।
इसी सम्मान में परशुराम ने वासुकी और सभी नागों को इस धरती का रक्षक बनाया।
script.description:
परशुराम जी ने फरसा फेंककर समुद्र से पश्चिमी तट कैसे निकाला, जानिए इस पौराणिक कथा में।
ऐसी ही और भारतीय कथाओं के लिए चैनल से जुड़ें।
claims_en: According to legend, Parashurama pushed back the sea with his axe.
Parashurama is the sixth avatar of Vishnu.
According to legend, he threw his axe into the Arabian Sea from Salher fort in Maharashtra.
According to the Kerala legend, water receded from Gokarna to Kanyakumari and new land emerged.
The land that emerged from the sea was filled with salt.
It was impossible to settle on that salty land.
Parashurama invoked the snake king Vasuki to save the land.
Vasuki's holy poison made the barren land fertile and lush green.
Out of respect, Parashurama appointed Vasuki and all snakes as protectors of the land.
scenes: Extreme close-up of Parashurama's face at the peak of fierce determination, matted locks and traditional tilak on his forehead, intense eyes reflecting bright coastal sunlight and ocean spray, traditional sage-warrior attire, cinematic illustrated still.

Wide dynamic illustrated shot of Parashurama in traditional dhoti and upper garment standing atop the rocky summit of Salher fort in Maharashtra, hurling his battle axe far out toward the sparkling Arabian Sea below under clear morning light.

Sweeping aerial illustrated view of the Arabian Sea waves receding dramatically along the western coast from Gokarna to Kanyakumari, revealing fresh wet earth rising from the ocean under warm golden sunlight.

Medium illustrated shot of Parashurama standing on the newly emerged shoreline, looking down with furrowed brow and concern at the pale white salt-crusted barren ground stretching before him in bright midday light.
Over-the-shoulder illustrated shot of Parashurama gazing quietly across the empty, lifeless salty plain with no trees or habitation, muted somber tones emphasizing the lonely stillness.

Medium illustrated shot of Parashurama standing on the coastal earth with palms joined respectfully in invocation, looking calmly at the radiant serpent king Vasuki emerging from soft mist before him at dusk.

Wide illustrated view of glowing emerald-golden mist flowing from Vasuki across the coastal plain, transforming the pale salty soil into lush green tropical groves, palm trees, and fertile fields under vibrant sunlight.

Medium-wide dignified illustrated shot of Parashurama smiling serenely with one hand raised in blessing toward Vasuki and sacred serpents gliding peacefully among lush green trees in warm golden hour light.
